sources.title: Peter Kramer1966 — The behavior of the rock crab Grapsus grapsus on Galapagos
sources.scope: Actual scanned pages18–20 rendered and read: slow forward/oblique versus fast sideways travel and empty-chela-to-mouth gestures. Historical subspecies suggestion is not adopted as a new accession. No trajectory, speed, force or social-signal fit.

retrieval.accessMethod: CDF PDF downloaded; selected actual pages rendered/read

sources.title: Galapagos Conservation Trust — Sally Lightfoot crab
sources.scope: Regional institutional species account supports selected adult blue/red/ochre phenotype and shore ecology. Not an individual museum determination, calibrated texture or complete native-range boundary.

shape.before: The earlier withheld oval/rod-limbed draft is preserved on the body sheet.
shape.changed: A lower rounded shell, thicker continuous sidewall, widely separated short eye stalks, eight broad flattened articulated walking legs, shorter dark joint caps and paired red chelae with pale distal tips replace the oval and rod-limbed draft.
shape.remaining: The regional shell outline, frontal lobes, orbital sockets, flattened limb cross sections and fine mouthparts are incomplete or unmeasured. Front carriage still differs from the selected photo. Pigment placement remains illustrative, with no sex/age determination, measured optics or full natural variation.

surface.changed: Selected red marginal, blue central and ochre pigment fields, fine cuticle relief, distal setae and red chelae are original numerical approximations guided by the authentic Galapagos photograph.
surface.remaining: Original numerical illustration, without calibrated optics, scan or full natural variation. The regional shell outline, frontal lobes, orbital sockets, flattened limb cross sections and fine mouthparts are incomplete or unmeasured. Front carriage still differs from the selected photo. Pigment placement remains illustrative, with no sex/age determination, measured optics or full natural variation.

movement.changed: Short authored forward support bout, separate lateral bout, local chela handling/opening and quiet support remain on the same meshes. No implemented swimming, empty-chela ingestion mechanism or calibrated running.
movement.remaining: No measured coordinates, natural playback rate, joint limits, forces, fluid dynamics, muscle, food contact, ingestion, sensory physiology or independent biological validation. Fixed-length/support checks establish internal software consistency only.

sourceAssessment: Actual scanned Kramer1966 pages18–20 were rendered/read. Slow forward/oblique walking is distinguished from rapid lateral travel; the separate lateral study is not a measured running gait. The Galapagos Conservation Trust account and Nosferattus CC0 photograph were compared. The historical subspecies proposal is not adopted as an accession.
fixesAfterRenderedReview: Reduced excessively high knees and pale joint caps after the first front/side comparison.
Increased shell convexity and replaced flat front plates with a continuous curved wall; darkened the blue ventral field.
Kept slow forward and lateral controls separate; no portunid paddles introduced.

assessmentRubric.texture: Distinct selected numerical surface; optics and microanatomy remain illustrative
assessmentRubric.movement: Working qualitative supported articulation; empirical rate/dynamics unvalidated
